Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

noah also noticed that a few names have alternate spellings on the backs of the prints his grandfather is written as frank on some cards and francis on others do not merge those labels yet because june is checking the family tree and has not decided whether they refer to the same person the importer can display both names for now and we can attach a note to the folder instead of editing every image there are six cards with this issue in the lake trip box and three more in the holiday folder so please mention the counts without treating them as confirmed errors

june said quote i want to be able to find the photographs even if we do not know the exact year yet end quote that is why i would like the search page to accept a place name as well as a year but this is a request for a later update not something to add to saturday's test for the test itself we only need the existing search fields and the proposed match list please do not tell her the place search has been added because nobody has started that work

after the test noah can send me the report as a plain text file and i will compare it with june's notebook on sunday if the report lists a suggested match please include the original filenames and the folder path so we can find them again if it lists no match leave that wording as it is rather than calling the photograph lost we have not checked every box and there may be scans on the second drive that are not copied into this archive yet

one last thing the family is bringing another album from the attic next month and june thinks it contains pictures from the old orchard but she is not certain about the year or who took them we should keep that album separate until she has looked through it and please leave space in the notes for what she remembers afterward i am not asking anyone to label those images now just make sure the importer can add them later without changing the older folders thanks that is everything i wanted to cover for saturday and the follow up report", "output": "Hi Mara, this is Elliot calling about the family photo importer we use for the Cedar Street archive, and I wanted to talk through the changes before we copy the next set of scans in on Saturday. My aunt June has been lending us the albums from her house, and my cousin Noah is checking the dates against the notes she wrote on the backs of the prints. The importer is useful, but it has started treating a few old folders differently after the laptop update, so I am dictating the details now while they are fresh. Could you make a clean transcript for the project notes?

The main problem showed up with the box marked Lake Trip 1998. The scanner made two files for several photographs: one is a large TIFF, and the other is a smaller JPEG. The importer placed both in the same event even though the filenames are not identical. We found eleven pairs across four folders, and none of the pictures appear to be missing. I first thought the duplicate check was using the date only—no, wait, it compares the date and the camera sequence number, so that is not the whole explanation. The large file was scanned on Monday, and the smaller one came from a memory card copied last winter.

Please keep the original files in the archive and have the importer make its working copies in the review folder. The setting we use for that should stay enabled, and I do not want the scan source overwritten while we test the new matching rule. The exact key is on a line by itself here.
archive.retain_originals
When June asked what that meant, I told her, “The importer can sort the copies without changing the pictures we got from you.” She said that sounded fine, but asked us to check that the pencil notes are still readable in the large scans.

For the test report, use the following list from Noah and keep each item separate:
1. Compare the file date with the date written in the notebook and flag a difference instead of choosing one automatically.
2. Check whether the camera sequence number is present in both files, and leave the pair for review if either value is missing.
3. Show the folder name next to each proposed match so June can recognize the trip without opening every image.
4. Do not count a TIFF and JPEG as a confirmed duplicate just because their subjects look alike.

There are a couple of practical details for Saturday. We have three volunteers and two laptops, but only one card reader that fits the older camera. I can bring the spare reader from my office if it still works, and Noah said he will bring the blue drive with the winter copies on it. The drive has about six hundred files, and the Cedar Street archive has roughly fourteen thousand images already, so we should run the sample on a small folder first rather than leave both laptops processing the full collection.

Mara, please use the folder called Porch Test for the first pass. It has twenty-four images from the same afternoon, and June remembers who is in each one. The folder was made last month and has not been edited since then. If the match screen looks sensible, we can try the Lake Trip folder next, but only after June has checked the larger scans for the notes. She specifically wants us to keep the labels that say who lent each album because two of the boxes came from neighbors rather than relatives.

There is one condition that matters for the later import: if the notebook date and the scan date disagree by more than one day, keep the notebook date as a suggested event date but leave the record marked “needs review.” If they differ by one day or less, show both dates and do not change the event automatically. Last time I said to just use the notebook date, but that was too broad because June sometimes wrote the date she developed a roll rather than the day she took the pictures. Please use this updated rule for the sample, and make clear in the notes that it applies only when both dates are available.

Noah also noticed that a few names have alternate spellings on the backs of the prints. His grandfather is written as Frank on some cards and Francis on others. Do not merge those labels yet because June is checking the family tree and has not decided whether they refer to the same person. The importer can display both names for now, and we can attach a note to the folder instead of editing every image. There are six cards with this issue in the Lake Trip box and three more in the Holiday folder, so please mention the counts without treating them as confirmed errors.

June said, “I want to be able to find the photographs even if we do not know the exact year yet.” That is why I would like the search page to accept a place name as well as a year, but this is a request for a later update, not something to add to Saturday’s test. For the test itself, we only need the existing search fields and the proposed match list. Please do not tell her the place search has been added because nobody has started that work.

After the test, Noah can send me the report as a plain text file, and I will compare it with June’s notebook on Sunday. If the report lists a suggested match, please include the original filenames and the folder path so we can find them again. If it lists no match, leave that wording as it is rather than calling the photograph lost. We have not checked every box, and there may be scans on the second drive that are not copied into this archive yet.

One last thing: the family is bringing another album from the attic next month, and June thinks it contains pictures from the old orchard, but she is not certain about the year or who took them. We should keep that album separate until she has looked through it, and please leave space in the notes for what she remembers afterward. I am not asking anyone to label those images now; just make sure the importer can add them later without changing the older folders. Thanks, that is everything I wanted to cover for Saturday and the follow-up report."}]
